sectors.ai: Buy YELO and ELIT on momentum, but rotate into INET and AREA for sustained earnings visibility as US tech weakness filters through. Trim EPAC and PMUI into strength—their gains lack volume confirmation. Keep net exposure neutral; the ID/US divergence signals local liquidity support, not a fundamental re-rating. Add on any pullback to 5-day moving averages.

sectors.name: Renewables & Climate-Tech
themes: Indonesia's renewable energy law and captive-market PPAs are structurally accelerating domestic project wins for local EPC and IPP players, decoupling them from global rate cycles.
US climate-tech names remain hostage to Fed policy and IRA uncertainty, making them tactical trades rather than core holdings until election-year clarity emerges.
Southeast Asia's grid interconnection and geothermal/bioenergy mandates are creating durable, multi-year revenue visibility for Indonesian operators, unlike commoditized solar manufacturing.
sectors.ai: Buy dips in Indonesian renewables names (LAPD, POWR, ESSA) as domestic policy tailwinds and tariff stability outweigh US-driven volatility; rotate out of US-exposed climate-tech until the Fed signals a clear cut. Prioritize local project pipelines and PPAs over equipment makers, and trim AWK/KEEN for liquidity into strength.

sectors.name: Consumer & FMCG
themes: Indonesia's consumer sector is benefiting from resilient domestic spending and food/beverage demand, which supports small-cap FMCG rallies despite macro headwinds.
Liquidity rotation into low-float, high-momentum consumer names (SRSN, KICI, OILS) signals speculative but durable trading patterns in Jakarta's retail-driven market.
US-linked FMCG exposure is underperforming ID peers, reflecting divergent consumer confidence and currency dynamics, favoring local-currency revenue plays.
sectors.ai: Buy selective small-cap FMCG names with confirmed volume and earnings catalysts (SRSN, KICI, OILS) while avoiding laggards; the sector's aggregate gain is thin, so rotate into ID-listed winners with domestic-demand exposure and exit US-linked names. Watch for profit-taking after sharp moves and add on pullbacks to strong charts.
